finding.claim: Open redirect (protocol-relative) in getRedirectUrl: a request path beginning with '/.' followed by slashes is normalized by the WHATWG URL parser into '//host/...', so the Location header becomes protocol-relative. Severity LOW: the attacker can only choose a host name that equals an existing directory name under root, and only when redirect:true. PLAUSIBLE, not executed.
finding.source: Request-target URL req.raw.url, e.g. GET /.//assets (attacker-controlled, index.js:144 and 157)
finding.sink: reply.redirect(getRedirectUrl(req.raw.url), 301) emitting a Location header (index.js:319 for directories, index.js:157 for the prefix route)

Non-leading '..' check does not match a single '.' segment, so it passes
send() normalizes './/assets' to 'assets' and returns type 'directory' when that directory exists
redirect branch calls getRedirectUrl(request.raw.url)
Only leading '/' and '\\' runs are collapsed; the '/.' prefix is not stripped
Result is '/' + './/assets' = '/.//assets'
new URL('/.//assets', 'http://localhost.com/').pathname is '//assets' (single-dot segment dropped, empty segment kept)
Returns '//assets/' as the Location

finding.guards_checked: Leading-slash collapse at index.js:786-790 (does not cover '/.' prefix). Traversal guard index.js:262 (not triggered). redirect option must be true (index.js:317). Redirect only fires for an existing directory (index.js:302-319). Impact limited to directory names as hostnames.

finding.claim: Insecure default: dotfiles defaults to 'allow', so with the default wildcard route any dotfile under root (e.g. .env, .git/config) is served to unauthenticated clients when the root directory contains them. MEDIUM, configuration-dependent. Also, list mode does not hide dotfiles unless dotfiles is 'deny' or 'ignore' (lib/dirList.js:83-84).

finding.guards_checked: No dotfile check in the wildcard route (index.js:137-154). The type declares 'allow'|'deny'|'ignore' (types/index.d.ts:66,117) with no secure default. Traversal guard is unrelated. Exploitable only when the served root contains dotfiles with secrets.

finding.claim: Existence oracle outside root for index files when preCompressed is enabled: a leading '..' request bypasses the traversal check, and findIndexFile stats a path outside root. The 404 vs 403 response difference reveals whether '<parent of root>/index.html' (or deeper ancestors) exists. LOW, information disclosure only; no file content is served.

finding.sink: statSync inside findIndexFile (index.js:588) reached via path.join(root, pathname, filename) with a pathname containing leading '..'

finding.guards_checked: Non-leading '..' guard index.js:262 (exempts leading '..' by design). @fastify/send's UP_PATH guard (returns 403, not content). Only when preCompressed is true (index.js:273). Confirmed only by reading; no file content is exposed.

finding.claim: Unbounded recursive directory walk on an unauthenticated request when list.extendedFolderInfo is enabled: each listed subdirectory triggers a full recursive walk via fs.stat (which follows symlinks) with no depth limit or visited-set. A symlink cycle in root makes the walk non-terminating. LOW to MEDIUM availability (DoS amplification). Precondition: extendedFolderInfo:true; the cycle case also needs an attacker-created symlink.

finding.sink: Recursive fs walk in dirList._getExtendedInfo (lib/dirList.js:41) started from dirList.list (lib/dirList.js:99-101)

finding.guards_checked: fastq concurrency (lib/dirList.js:12, 49) only bounds parallelism, not depth or total work. No depth or symlink guard. Traversal guard isPathInsideRoot (lib/dirList.js:14-22) applies only to the listed dir, not the recursive walk. Option is off by default.

finding.claim: Fire-and-forget async call: pumpSendToReply is invoked without await or catch from the wildcard handler (and from sendFile/download decorators at index.js:102 and 123). Any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which crashes the Node process by default. I did not find a concrete attacker-triggerable throw, so this is a latent robustness risk, not a confirmed DoS. LOW, PLAUSIBLE.
